title: Coherent chart prescription on finite admissible embedded histories
statement: Fix a marked-ideal numerical resolution R [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine]. There is a simultaneous family ν of values in ResolutionWord on all finite embedded histories [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history] such that, for every history H admissible relative to ν: (i) every singular point x admits a ResolutionWordChart R H x [def-trf-resolution-word-charts]; (ii) for every point x and every such chart C, ν H x equals C.word; (iii) ν H x is bottom if and only if its intrinsic local ring is regular. The assignment and charts use no auxiliary global dimension bound. No finite-image, closed-upper-level or summation-comparison assertion is made.

proof.text: The hypotheses used below (reduced and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$) hold at every stage of an admissible history, by induction on its length. The initial scheme of an embedded pair is reduced and of finite type, and the target of a smooth comparison is a history of another embedded pair whose centers are the extended ideals of the given ones. At a maximum extension the ambient $P_H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so the reduced ideal of the center $C$ is of finite type. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with center ideal $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, the Rees algebra of [def-nagata-affine-blowup] is generated over $A$ by $a_1t,\ldots,a_rt$; hence its $\operatorname{Proj}$ is covered by the finitely many $D_+(a_it)$, whose degree-zero rings are generated by the $a_j/a_i$. Thus the glued blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and so is its closed subscheme $X_{H+1}$. By [def-nagata-strict-transform], $X_{H+1}$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of the open part over $P_H\setminus C$, which is isomorphic to an open subscheme of the reduced $X_H$; so $X_{H+1}$ is reduced by [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image]. Use [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile] at the current reduced finite-type stage. Its normalized head is precisely $A_x$, with regular value $a_{\rm reg}=(1,(1,1,\ldots))$ and all singular heads strictly greater. Choose a dimension bound $D$ only for this verification. The modified head $B_D=(c,\Lambda^D\Delta^q h)$ has finite image and closed upper levels. The integer_operators assertion of the dimension-profile dependency identifies its comparisons with those of $A$, so $A$ itself has these properties. Its regular level is open: if there are singular values, exclude the closed upper level of the least of the finitely many singular heads. When there are none this open is the whole stage.

proof.text: For each singular pointed germ choose the Hilbert--Samuel presentation of [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations], in a minimal smooth envelope, with support equal to that envelope and order exactly its marking on cosupport. The head theorem identifies the head-level tests with these Hilbert--Samuel tests, so this presents the local head stratum as well. Keep the earlier center ideals and exceptional births as history, while starting the test boundary empty. For two choices, [lem-trf-minimal-envelope-coefficient-comparison] gives a common pointed etale comparison preserving those earlier ideals and identifies their entire finite-test classes, including the displayed codimension-zero suspensions. At an identified pointed germ, minimal envelopes have equal support dimension: their cotangent dimensions equal that of the germ and their residue transcendence degrees agree. Thus the fixed-support-dimension hypothesis for tail invariance applies. This compares presentations, not their actual coefficient ideals.

proof.text: Apply the fixed simultaneous assignment of [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] to these maximal-order presentations. Their words have leading $1$; remove that entry and call the result $t$. Equivalent presentations with the identified ordered histories of the preceding pointed comparisons have equal tails. The same applies after restriction to overlaps and common etale comparisons. Consequently $(A,t)$ has one value at every singular point, independent of the choices. Equality on pairwise comparisons is transitive, so there is no additional cocycle choice. Use the product lexicographic order of the head space with the engine's fixed tail space, and adjoin a new least element $\bot$. Assign $\bot$ at regular points. This uses neither the auxiliary $D$ nor a bound on the length of a resolution tower.

proof.text: The construction is simultaneous on finite histories, not an induction starting at the end of a tower. At length zero use the stagewise head, presentation and overlap constructions just described. Given the ordered data of a finite prefix, the local-presentation theorem identifies, after every allowed next test operation, the cosupport of its controlled ideal with the retaining-level locus on the scheme-theoretic strict transform. The head theorem gives the same retaining tests for the normalized head. On this locus, the engine's transformed word and any newly chosen equivalent presentation have equal tails, by its test-equivalence invariance and the history comparison of the preceding pointed comparisons. Where the old head has dropped the old presentation no longer has cosupport; choose a presentation of the new head there and apply the same rule. It would be incorrect to use a vanished old cosupport to present that lower level. Induction on the length of a finite prefix proves compatibility at every transformed stage. The definition [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history] then restricts these prescriptions to the least class closed under maximum extensions and smooth comparisons with deletion; restrictions and smooth pullbacks are among the engine's simultaneous histories. All choices at a given prefix depend only on that prefix's recorded ideals and births. No induction on an unknown terminating length, and no use of the later termination theorem, occurs. The regular prescription is bottom, whereas every chart at a singular point has a word constructed as some (head,tail), which is not bottom. This gives exactly the regularity equivalence. No topological assertion is used.

lean.statement:
theorem resolution_word_coherent_prescription (R : MarkedIdeal.NumericalResolution.{u}) :
    ∃ ν : ValueFamily.{u} HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord,
      ∀ {A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {n : ℕ} (H : EmbeddedResolutionHistory A n),
        Admissible ν H →
        (∀ x : H.X, ¬ IsRegularLocalRing (H.X.presheaf.stalk x) →
          Nonempty (ResolutionWordChart R H x)) ∧
        (∀ (x : H.X) (C : ResolutionWordChart R H x), ν H x = C.word) ∧
        (∀ x : H.X, ν H x = ⊥ ↔ IsRegularLocalRing (H.X.presheaf.stalk x))
